title: Why IndiGo is losing money even after raising fares

outro.text: The next clue lands December 1, when jet fuel is repriced. And that is why IndiGo's fares jumped a third

sources: IndiGo (InterGlobe Aviation) Q2 FY27 results filing and earnings call, Oct. 2026
Reuters / Business Standard coverage of IndiGo Q2 FY27 loss

scenes.hook_card: FARES +34%  |  STILL A Rs 1,879 cr LOSS
scenes.text: IndiGo's fares jumped 34 percent. It still lost 1,879 crore rupees.
That is its third losing quarter in a row. So where did the money go? Not the flying. The dollar.
Fuel, plane leases and engines are all priced in dollars, while tickets sell in rupees.

card.title: A $1,000 bill costs IndiGo
card.source: IndiGo Q2 FY27 filing, author calculation

scenes.text: A thousand-dollar bill cost 87,060 rupees a year ago. Now it costs about 95,090.

card.title: IndiGo Q2 FY27 loss, Rs million

scenes.text: Its own filing says, without currency effects, the loss was 7,237 million rupees. The reported loss was 18,791 million.

stat: rupees lost came from the currency
scenes.text: Six of every ten rupees lost came from the currency, not the flying.
